title: Feature flags with gradual rollout

requirements.text: A user gets the same result for a flag on every evaluation (deterministic hashing of flag key and user)
Raising the rollout percentage only adds users; nobody already enabled is dropped
Allow and deny lists override the percentage, and disabling a flag turns it off for everyone
Invalid flag keys, percentages and variant weights are rejected
Each evaluation reports the reason (and bucket) so decisions can be logged and debugged
Flag changes take effect without a deploy, from a server-side store the client cannot alter
Flags can be rolled out per tenant or organization as well as per user
Only authorized users can change flags, and changes are recorded

evidence.name: sticky bucketing: the same flag and user always give the same bucket, result and variant
monotonic rollout: raising the percentage only adds users and nobody already enabled is dropped
targeting precedence: kill switch > user deny > user allow > tenant deny > tenant allow > rollout, with reasons
config validation rejects invalid keys, percentages, variant weights, duplicates and unknown fields
explainable: every evaluation reports reason, bucket, version and variant source
runtime config: changes reach other instances after the TTL without a deploy, and subscribers are notified
SQL store: runtime config reaches a second instance after the TTL and notifies subscribers
tenant targeting: bucketBy tenant rolls a whole organization in or out together
audited changes: only authorized actors change flags, and each change records who, when, before and after
SQL store: audited CRUD with optimistic versions; the audit table is append-only

implementations.notes: Buckets use FNV-1a with a MurmurHash3 finalizer. PGlite tests run on one connection.
